newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isuzu may take over GM diesel engine output.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu may take over GM diesel engine output.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd said on Thursday that it and General Motors Corp of the United States are considering transferring GM's diesel engine development and production to Isuzu.
Isuzu also said the two companies had agreed that Isuzu will produce 1,700cc diesel engines at its Poland factory for GM affiliate Adam Opel AG starting in 2000.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Thursday that the companies had agreed that Isuzu would make diesel engines in the United States to be supplied to GM and that Isuzu would develop diesel-powered commercial vehicles.
The leading U.S. automaker holds a 37.4 percent stake in Isuzu.
An Isuzu spokesman said, however, that no agreement had been reached on diesel engine production in the U.S. or on diesel-powered vehicle development for GM.
Isuzu announced in May that it had signed a deal with the Polish government under which it will invest 200 million marks by mid-1999 to build an engine factory in southern Poland.
The company also said at that time that it planned to start production there by the summer of 1999, with annual output of 200,000 engines in 1999 and 300,000 in 2000.
